title: Large Language Models: A Survey
extended_summary:
This paper is a broad survey of large language models (LLMs), motivated by the rapid rise of ChatGPT and related models. It does not investigate an educational intervention or student outcomes; instead, it synthesizes recent advances in LLM architectures, training methods, alignment techniques, datasets, evaluation benchmarks, and applications. The survey covers major LLM families such as GPT, LLaMA, and PaLM, and also discusses other representative models and emerging capabilities like in-context learning, instruction following, reasoning, and tool use.

The paper focuses on the technical development of LLMs, including pre-training, fine-tuning, RLHF, decoding strategies, data cleaning, tokenization, and augmentation with external knowledge or tools. It uses examples from general-purpose AI systems such as ChatGPT, GPT-4, and other LLMs, but these are discussed as model examples rather than as interventions studied in schools or classrooms.

Because this is a review article, it does not report a participant population, setting, experimental comparison, or outcome measures relevant to middle school mathematics achievement. Its main conclusion is that LLMs are rapidly advancing and have strong potential across many tasks, while still facing challenges related to efficiency, safety, multimodality, and responsible deployment.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a narrative survey of large language models, not an empirical study of ChatGPT or any educational intervention. It does not report a study design, sample, comparison group, or outcome data relevant to middle school mathematics achievement.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper provides no direct evidence of impact on K-12 mathematics achievement or any student outcome. It is background/review literature only, so no effect size or intervention impact can be inferred.
